_: A storage mechanism. No single curve identifies one, so the record has to say how to tell it from its neighbours.
name: Electrical double layer
summary: Charge is stored electrostatically in the layer of ions that assembles at the electrode surface. No electron crosses the interface, and no bond changes.
whatHappens: Applying a potential attracts counter-ions to the surface and repels co-ions, forming a compact layer of separated charge a few ion diameters thick. The charge is held by electrostatics alone, like a capacitor with a very small plate separation and a very large area.
whereChargeGoes: The surface, and only the surface. Storage scales with accessible area, not with volume.
inCV: A rectangle. Current is roughly constant across the window and reverses sign immediately at each vertex, because there is no reaction to wait for.
inGCD: A straight line. Voltage falls linearly with time, which is the definition of constant capacitance.
dQdV: Flat, or nearly so — the electrode takes roughly the same charge per volt everywhere in its window.
rateBehaviour: Fast. There is no charge-transfer step, so the rate limit is ion transport into the pores — which is why pore size and wetting dominate rate capability rather than any chemistry.
distinguishFrom: Versus surface pseudocapacitance: both give near-rectangular CVs, and that shape alone does NOT separate them. A double layer stores no charge faradaically, so its capacitance is largely insensitive to the redox chemistry of the electrolyte; a pseudocapacitive contribution disappears when the couple is removed. Comparing electrolytes, not curve shapes, is what separates them.
Versus battery-type: look at the discharge line. A genuine double layer is linear over the whole window; a plateau anywhere means charge is going somewhere else.
_distinguishFrom: REQUIRED — an error if absent, a warning with only one entry. Each entry names a neighbouring mechanism and the experiment that separates them.
quantityToReport: Capacitance (F, F/g, F/cm²) is meaningful here, because a single value describes the electrode across its whole window.
_quantityToReport: Which quantity may honestly be reported for this mechanism — capacitance in F/g, or capacity in mAh/g. Reporting the wrong one is the practical consequence of misidentifying it.
misread: Attributing all of a carbon electrode's capacitance to the double layer when surface functional groups are contributing faradaically
Explaining a capacitance difference by BET area alone — the accessible area, not the measured area, is what stores charge
degradation: Slow, because nothing is transformed. What fails is usually the electrolyte at the window edges, the binder, or the contact — not the carbon.
